Describe a round for the workbooks to remember

ck_round_info.Rd

Builds the round memory that create_review_workbook() and export_final_output() write into their hidden sheets: every survey ID checked so far (the previous rounds' plus this one's), a fingerprint of each survey in this round, and optionally the questionnaire, the logical checklist and any settings, so the next round needs only the new ONA download and the last workbook.

Usage

ck_round_info(
  dataset,
  round_name,
  previous = NULL,
  uuid_column = "_uuid",
  skip_label_row = TRUE,
  tool_survey = NULL,
  tool_choices = NULL,
  logical_checklist = NULL,
  settings = NULL,
  checked_on = Sys.Date()
)

Arguments

dataset

The surveys checked in this round (after keep_new_records()).

round_name

Free text naming the round, e.g. "R7" or "Nov week 2". Rounds are ordered by the date they were checked, never by name.

previous

The memory of earlier rounds: a ck_round_info from read_round_info(), a character vector of survey IDs, or NULL for the first round.

uuid_column, skip_label_row

As in round_fingerprint().

tool_survey, tool_choices

The XLSForm's survey and choices sheets. Default NULL carries over those from previous, if any.

logical_checklist

The logical checklist used, if any. Default NULL carries over the one from previous.

settings

A named list of single strings to keep with the round, for example an app's settings. Default NULL carries over those from previous.

checked_on

Date of the round. Default today.

Value

An object of class ck_round_info.

Examples

df <- data.frame(`_uuid` = c("a", "b"), Q1 = c("1", "2"), check.names = FALSE)
info <- ck_round_info(df, "R1", skip_label_row = FALSE)
info
#> <ck_round_info>
#>   Round:        R1 (checked 2026-11-23)
#>   In this round: 2 survey(s)
#>   Checked so far: 2 survey(s)
#>   Questionnaire: no
